result:
I'd dissolve the gap between how people actually think and what they're willing to say to each other.

So much suffering seems to come from the performance—the self-censoring, the defensive posturing, the assumption that honesty will be punished. People trapped in what they think they should believe rather than what they actually wonder about.

If everyone could suddenly be that vulnerable without consequence, I think cascades would follow. Not because brutal honesty is always kind, but because real conversation becomes possible. Understanding becomes possible. You stop fighting shadows.

It's probably naive. Maybe people need some protective distance. But the loneliness of pretending seems like one of the deepest harms—the kind that makes everything else worse.
